title: A Wondrous Star Our Pioneer
description: A Wondrous Star Our Pioneer in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 7 verses and a piano.
about: John Weiss wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 424, “Epiphany”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: A won-drous star our pi-o-neer, We left the mys-tic land Where hea-ven nur-tured child-hood slept, Where yet old vi-sions stand.

lines: A wondrous star our pioneer,
We left the mystic land
Where heaven-nurtured childhood slept,
Where yet old visions stand.
O God! the land of dreams we left,
Repose we left for aye,
And followed meekly to the place
Where our Redeemer lay.
That humble manger we have found;
The world his cradle is;
His life is hidden far below
Its sins and miseries.
The world throws wide its brazen gates;
With Thee we enter in;
O, grant us, in our humble sphere,
To free that world from sin.
We have one mind in Christ our Lord
To stand and point above;
To hurl rebuke at social wrong;
But all, O God, in love.
The star is resting in the sky;
To worship Christ we came;
The moments haste; O, touch our tongues
With Thy celestial flame!
The truest worship is a life;
All dreaming we resign;
We lay our offerings at thy feet, —
Our lives, O Christ, are thine!

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: John Weiss died in 1879.
credits: Words by John Weiss (1818–1879), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
